table.title: Courier Delivery Commitments by Destination
table.html:
DestinationDelivery
WindowConditions
Metro Manila2–3 daysOrders confirmed before 14:00 on a business day are dispatched the same day; deliveries to gated communities may require recipient confirmation at the lobby, which can add up to one business day.
Greater Luzon3–4 daysService covers municipalities with a permanent courier route; barangays classified as remote by the operator are served twice weekly, and road closures caused by typhoons may suspend delivery without prior notice.
Visayas3–5 daysShipments travel by roll-on/roll-off vessel or air freight depending on volume, and inter-island transfers can be delayed by port congestion or adverse weather; tracking updates are issued at each handover point.
Mindanao4–6 daysCoverage includes major cities and selected municipal hubs, while addresses outside confirmed service areas are held at the nearest branch for customer pickup; delivery attempts are made on business days only.
Remote island areas5–7 daysDeliveries depend on scheduled boat trips and local transport availability, and the courier may contact the recipient to arrange a meeting point; additional storage charges apply after five calendar days at the destination branch.
table.brief: Two columns under one group header with very different content: "Delivery" group with "Window" (short like 2–3 days) and "Conditions" (long sentences)

understanding.purpose: Communicate delivery time commitments and their qualifying conditions for each destination.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a destination, scan across to its delivery window, and read the conditions; they may also compare windows down the column. Long conditions will set much of the row height, leaving room for destination names to wrap within the same rows.
groups: Window and Conditions belong under Delivery: the first gives the promised time range and the second qualifies it.
Destination identifies each row and anchors the comparison.
keep_intact: Delivery window values such as 2–3 days
Individual words and identifiers, including place names and time expressions
may_wrap: Multiword destination names at word spaces
Conditions prose at natural word boundaries

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Give Destination slightly more room than r2A to test whether Greater Luzon can stay on one line, while preserving a substantial Conditions column and intact delivery windows.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Widen Destination modestly from r0B to ease label wrapping while retaining nearly all of its generous conditions width.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Explore a stronger row-label anchor with a two-line longest destination, while reclaiming the excess window width seen in r0C for Conditions.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Test a small increase in destination width from r1B to see whether Greater Luzon can stay on one line while retaining most of its conditions width.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give conditions more space while retaining enough text width for the longest unbreakable destination word; multiword destinations can wrap naturally within the tall rows.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Test the alternative of keeping every destination on one line, including Remote island areas, and assess whether that scanning benefit justifies narrower conditions.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Refine r2B by returning 7px to Destination, aiming to make wrapped labels less cramped while retaining most of the width gained for conditions.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Use r2B's allocation as the prose-first benchmark: its minimum destination width preserves the longest individual word and gives conditions the most room among the tested designs.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The short delivery windows would occupy excessive space, leaving the conditions in a narrow column with many short lines and making each row harder to scan.
bad.why: The short delivery windows would occupy excessive space, leaving the conditions in a narrow column with many short lines and making each row harder to scan.

rationale: r3A keeps Metro Manila and Greater Luzon on one line, making the destination column easy to scan, while Remote island areas wraps naturally onto two lines. The delivery windows remain intact, and the conditions have enough width for readable phrases despite the long text. The extra line in the Mindanao conditions is a reasonable cost for clearer row labels.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading role; equal columns can waste space when their contents differ substantially.
Keep row identifiers and compact values easy to scan while giving prose enough width to form readable lines.
Judge wrapping by its effect on reading and row relationships, not by table height alone.
specific: A 92px window column fits the header and delivery ranges on one line.
Around 137px for destinations keeps both Metro Manila and Greater Luzon on one line, while the long conditions still receive most of the width.

tradeoffs: r2B and r3C give conditions more room and reduce table height, but wrap Metro Manila and Greater Luzon and spread Remote island areas over three lines. r1C and r2C make destination labels more spacious at the cost of narrower, more heavily wrapped conditions.
uncertain: The ranges are narrow estimates based on the supplied renders; intermediate widths were not rendered. A designer who prioritizes compact prose over scanning destination names could reasonably prefer r2B or r3C.

critique.good: All destination names and delivery windows stay on one line. The headers are clear, and words remain intact.
critique.problems: The conditions form narrow, tall blocks, while the destination column has substantial unused space below its short labels. The large row heights make comparisons down the window column less convenient.
critique.cause: Destination receives 182px, enough for its longest label on one line, leaving only 239px for the much longer conditions.

critique.good: The wider conditions column creates readable prose and shorter rows. Windows stay on one line, and the compact table makes destinations and commitments easier to compare.
critique.problems: Metro Manila and Greater Luzon wrap, and Remote island areas breaks across three lines. The narrow destination column makes the row labels feel cramped beside the much wider conditions.
critique.cause: At 113px, Destination has only 92px of text space. Conditions receives 308px, so some of that width could be returned to the row labels.

critique.good: Most destination names stay on one line, and Remote island areas wraps naturally onto two. Headers and window values remain intact.
critique.problems: The window column has conspicuous unused space, while the conditions are narrow and rows are tall. This weakens the balance between the short commitments and the prose that qualifies them.
critique.cause: Window receives 125px even though its one-line content needs 92px including padding; that extra width leaves Conditions at 243px.

critique.good: Destination labels are easy to scan, delivery windows stay on one line, and the grouped headers are clear. Only the longest destination wraps, naturally, while conditions remain readable.
critique.problems: Conditions occupy seven or eight lines per row, making the table tall and leaving substantial empty space beneath the short labels and windows.
critique.cause: The 140px destination column preserves Greater Luzon on one line but leaves 281px for the much longer conditions.

critique.good: The wider conditions column produces the most compact table and makes the prose easier to follow. Windows and headers remain intact, and wrapped destination labels stay within their rows.
critique.problems: Greater Luzon wraps, weakening the quick scan of destination names. The first row is shorter than the others, although the overall row rhythm remains orderly.
critique.cause: The 125px destination column gives conditions 296px, but its 104px text area is too narrow for Greater Luzon on one line.

critique.good: Most destination names are prominent and easy to scan; windows and the header hierarchy remain clear.
critique.problems: The conditions are noticeably narrow, producing eight or nine lines per row and a much taller table. Remote island areas still wraps, so the extra destination width does not keep every label on one line.
critique.cause: The 160px destination column leaves only 261px for conditions, without providing the 182px needed for the longest destination on one line.

critique.good: The destination column gives most labels a comfortable shape, while the windows remain intact and easy to compare. Conditions read in reasonably sized lines, and each row is clearly associated with its destination.
critique.problems: The condition text still runs to seven lines in four rows, making the table tall. Greater Luzon wraps despite having only two words, while much of the destination column remains empty below each label.
critique.cause: At 132px, Destination has 111px of text space, enough for Metro Manila but not Greater Luzon on one line. The 289px Conditions column has 268px of text space, so its prose determines the row heights.

critique.good: The wider Conditions column makes the prose easier to scan and reduces several rows to six lines. Windows and headers remain intact, and the table retains clear row boundaries.
critique.problems: Metro Manila and Greater Luzon both split across two lines, and Remote island areas occupies three, weakening the destination column as a quick index. The first column feels cramped beside the expansive conditions.
critique.cause: The 113px Destination column leaves only 92px for text. Moving those 19px to Conditions gives it 287px of text space and improves prose wrapping.

critique.good: Every destination appears on one line, giving the row labels a clear, consistent rhythm. The delivery windows and all headers also remain intact.
critique.problems: Conditions are broken into many short lines, including an awkward break within the hyphenated roll-on/roll-off expression. The resulting tall rows leave large empty areas under the short destination and window entries and make comparisons across rows harder.
critique.cause: The 182px Destination column is wide enough for the longest label on one line, but leaves Conditions only 239px, or 218px of text space.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: Equal-width columns leave excessive space around the short delivery windows and squeeze the conditions into narrow, heavily wrapped passages. The resulting tall rows make comparisons harder.

ref_auto.why: Conditions have a comfortable measure, but every delivery window splits the number from ‘days’, and several destination names wrap. This weakens scanning of the two identifying columns.

r1C.why: Delivery windows stay on one line and most destinations do too. Conditions are readable, though the wider destination column leaves the prose somewhat more constrained than in D or E.

r1B.why: The conditions column is spacious and all delivery windows stay intact. Greater Luzon and Remote island areas wrap, slightly slowing the scan of destinations.

r3A.why: All delivery windows and all but the longest destination stay on one line, while conditions have ample space. The column proportions support both quick comparison and reading the qualifications.

ref_equal.why: As in A, the broad window column wastes space while the conditions wrap into narrow, lengthy blocks. Large empty areas beside the prose make the rows harder to scan as units.

raw.unsure: D is a close alternative: it gives conditions slightly more room, while E keeps Greater Luzon on one line.

ref_equal.why: Equal-width columns give the short delivery windows excessive space and squeeze conditions into narrow, tall blocks, making rows harder to scan.

contrast.why: The equal-width columns leave substantial empty space beside the windows while conditions wrap into long, narrow blocks.

r3A.why: Delivery windows and most destinations stay on one line, while conditions have enough width for comfortable reading. The columns fit their different roles well.

ref_auto.why: Conditions read comfortably, but every delivery window breaks before ‘days’ and several destinations wrap, weakening quick comparison.

r1C.why: Destinations and delivery windows are easy to scan, though conditions wrap more often than in C and the destination column has some spare space.

r1B.why: Conditions have generous, readable lines and delivery windows stay intact, though Greater Luzon and Remote island areas wrap.

raw.unsure: C and F are close; the choice depends on how much weight is given to keeping destination names on one line versus giving conditions slightly more width.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
